app_name: Cap Fund Academy — Buffer Social Automation
description: Cap Fund Academy publishes daily AI-generated social media content to LinkedIn, Instagram, and TikTok via Buffer. Posts cover rural capital access, USDA microlending programs (RMAP, RBDG, IRP), and government lending certifications. Content is AI-authored, compliance-reviewed, and queued automatically through Buffer's MCP server.

get_account.description: Retrieve the authenticated Buffer account's profile information including user ID, email, and plan details.

justifications.read_only_justification: This tool only reads account metadata from Buffer's API. It does not create, modify, or delete any data.
justifications.destructive_justification: No data is altered or removed. This is a pure read operation that fetches existing account information.
justifications.open_world_justification: The account is connected to public social media platforms (LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok). Account data reflects the state of those publicly registered profiles.

list_channels.description: List all social media channels connected to the Buffer account, including their IDs, platform types, and connection status.

justifications.read_only_justification: This tool only retrieves the list of connected channels. No channel connections are added, modified, or removed.
justifications.destructive_justification: No data is deleted or irreversibly changed. The tool fetches the existing channel list without mutation.
justifications.open_world_justification: Each channel represents a public social media profile (e.g. a LinkedIn page, Instagram account) that exists on the open internet.

get_channel.description: Retrieve detailed metadata for a specific Buffer channel by its ID, including platform, handle, avatar, and posting configuration.

justifications.read_only_justification: This tool fetches a single channel's metadata without making any changes to it.
justifications.destructive_justification: No data is modified or deleted. This is a read-only GET operation against Buffer's API.
justifications.open_world_justification: The channel corresponds to a public social media account. Its metadata (handle, avatar, platform) reflects publicly accessible information about that account.

list_posts.description: List queued, scheduled, sent, or draft posts for a given Buffer channel, with filtering by status and date range.

justifications.read_only_justification: This tool only reads posts from the Buffer queue. No posts are created, modified, or deleted by this operation.
justifications.destructive_justification: No existing data is altered. Posts listed are not affected by the retrieval operation.
justifications.open_world_justification: Posts in the queue are intended for publication on public social media platforms. Sent posts are already publicly visible content.

get_post.description: Retrieve the full details of a single Buffer post by its ID, including content, scheduling time, channel, and publish status.

justifications.read_only_justification: This tool retrieves one post's data without modifying it in any way.
justifications.destructive_justification: The post is not changed, deleted, or rescheduled by this operation. It is a pure read.
justifications.open_world_justification: The post is either already published publicly or is scheduled to be. Its content represents material intended for public social media audiences.

create_idea.description: Create a new content idea or draft in Buffer's idea storage, which can later be converted into a scheduled post.

justifications.read_only_justification: This tool writes a new idea record to Buffer. It is not read-only because it creates new data.
justifications.destructive_justification: Creating an idea is an additive operation. It does not overwrite or remove any existing ideas or posts, and can be deleted or discarded later.
justifications.open_world_justification: An idea is a precursor to a social media post. Once converted and published, it will become publicly visible content on LinkedIn, Instagram, or TikTok.

create_post.description: Create and queue a new social media post in Buffer for a specified channel. The post is added to the scheduling queue and published at the designated time.

justifications.read_only_justification: This tool creates a new post entry in Buffer's queue. It writes data and is therefore not read-only.
justifications.destructive_justification: Creating a queued post is additive and non-destructive. The post can be edited or deleted before it publishes. No existing posts or data are overwritten.
justifications.open_world_justification: Once the scheduled time arrives, Buffer publishes the post publicly to the connected social media platform (LinkedIn, Instagram, or TikTok), making it visible to the public.

edit_post.description: Edit the content, media, or scheduled time of an existing Buffer post that has not yet been published.

justifications.read_only_justification: This tool modifies an existing post's content or schedule. It writes to Buffer's API and is not read-only.
justifications.destructive_justification: Editing a post overwrites its previous content. The original version of the post text, media, or schedule is permanently replaced and cannot be recovered after the edit is saved.
justifications.open_world_justification: The edited post will be published to a public social media platform at its scheduled time. Changes to content directly affect what will appear publicly.

delete_post.description: Permanently delete a queued or draft Buffer post before it is published.

justifications.read_only_justification: This tool removes a post from Buffer's queue. It is a write operation and is not read-only.
justifications.destructive_justification: Deletion permanently removes the post from Buffer's queue. The post and all its content are unrecoverable after deletion. This action cannot be undone.
justifications.open_world_justification: Although the post has not yet been published, it was intended for a public social media platform. Deletion affects the planned public content pipeline for LinkedIn, Instagram, or TikTok.

introspect_schema.description: Retrieve the GraphQL schema of Buffer's API, including available types, queries, mutations, and field definitions.

justifications.read_only_justification: This tool performs a schema introspection query, which only reads the API's type system definition. No data is created or modified.
justifications.destructive_justification: Schema introspection is a metadata read operation. It does not alter any posts, channels, or account data.
justifications.open_world_justification: The schema describes capabilities that interact with public social media platforms. Understanding the schema enables operations that affect publicly visible content.

execute_query.description: Execute a read-only GraphQL query against Buffer's API to retrieve data about posts, channels, analytics, or account information.

justifications.read_only_justification: GraphQL queries by definition only read data and do not modify state. This tool is restricted to query operations, not mutations.
justifications.destructive_justification: No data is created, updated, or deleted. This tool only retrieves existing data from Buffer's API via read-only queries.
justifications.open_world_justification: The data returned may include information about posts published or scheduled for public social media platforms, reflecting publicly visible content.

execute_mutation.description: Execute a GraphQL mutation against Buffer's API to create, update, or delete posts, ideas, or scheduling data.

justifications.read_only_justification: GraphQL mutations modify server-side state. This tool explicitly performs write operations and is not read-only.
justifications.destructive_justification: Mutations can make irreversible changes, including deleting posts, overwriting post content, or modifying channel settings. Some mutations cannot be undone after execution.
justifications.open_world_justification: Mutations can create, edit, or schedule content that will be published publicly on LinkedIn, Instagram, or TikTok, directly affecting what audiences see on those platforms.

test_prompts.prompt: Schedule a LinkedIn post for today about USDA RMAP microlending eligibility requirements.
What posts do I have queued for Instagram this week?
Delete the last post in my TikTok queue.

test_responses.prompt: Schedule a LinkedIn post for today about USDA RMAP microlending eligibility requirements.
test_responses.expected_response_summary: The assistant calls list_channels to find the LinkedIn channel ID, then calls create_post with the composed text and automatic queue scheduling. It confirms the post was queued and shows the estimated publish time.

test_responses.prompt: What posts do I have queued for Instagram this week?
test_responses.expected_response_summary: The assistant calls list_channels to get the Instagram channel ID, then calls list_posts filtered to queued status. It returns a list of upcoming posts with their scheduled publish times.

test_responses.prompt: Delete the last post in my TikTok queue.
test_responses.expected_response_summary: The assistant calls list_channels for the TikTok channel ID, calls list_posts to find the last queued post, then calls delete_post with that post's ID. It confirms the post was permanently deleted.

release_notes: Initial submission. Enables Cap Fund Academy to queue and manage daily AI-generated social media posts across LinkedIn, Instagram, and TikTok via Buffer's MCP server using OAuth 2.0 authentication.
